lines.text: You ask an AI a question. Seconds later, an answer.

lines.text: But it isn't pulling a finished reply from a file. It's predicting one, piece by piece.

lines.text: With popular AI chat apps, your message travels to computers in a data center, running a large language model.

lines.text: First, your text is split into tokens: small chunks like words, parts of words, or punctuation.

lines.text: During training, the model learned patterns from huge amounts of text. It doesn't look through that text when it answers. The patterns are captured in billions of numbers.

lines.text: Now it uses those patterns, and everything in the conversation, to calculate which token is likely to come next.

lines.text: It picks one, adds it, and repeats, token by token, until the answer is complete.

lines.text: That's why AI sounds so fluent. But fluent isn't the same as correct. It can sound confident and still be wrong.
